repo_notes.content: Tedix exists to protect human attention. People hand off work; Tedix brings back only the decisions that need a person, ranked by what matters most, and handles the rest. The same need applies to one developer running many coding assistants in parallel and to an operator choosing which contributions are worth their time. Open the Overview with that problem and outcome, not with architecture. Write in plain English for a developer seeing the project for the first time. Do not describe Tedix as AI coworkers, AI workers, a to-do list or a governance platform. Define product terms once where they first appear: a tedi is a persistent worker with its own memory, skills and permissions; a Work Item is one unit of handed-off work with an owner, a risk level and a budget; Home is the entry point that answers directly or hands work to a tedi; Decisions shows the decisions waiting for a person; Activity shows results that need no decision. Prefer current code and docs/public over older prose, and docs/public/release-status.md for what is available today. Never name customers or tenants; examples use fictional organizations.

The repository is built in the open by coding agents that Tedix itself coordinates. Commits carry Work-Item and Agent-Session trailers that link each change to its task and agent session; the ids do not resolve publicly. Pull requests are disabled: outside contributors and their agents open an issue (optionally with a diff) or follow AGENT-REVIEW.md, and maintainers re-author accepted changes with credit. Explain this once on the contribution page rather than on every page.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: The problem Tedix solves (people spend attention on work that does not need them), the outcome it delivers, the main concepts, how the pieces fit together on Cloudflare, and links to every section.

pages.title: Getting Started Locally
pages.purpose: bun run-local: prerequisites, what it starts, local organization setup, optional Workers AI inference, --smoke and --demo, and where local data lives.

pages.title: Repository Layout
pages.purpose: apps/, packages/, plugins/, scripts/, docs/public/, decisions/ and examples/; how workspaces depend on each other; the AGENTS.md hard invariants (no db.transaction, contracts in packages/api-contract, no barrel files, config in D1 rows).

pages.title: How Contributions Work
pages.purpose: Agent-built development: commit trailers, the push queue and pre-push gates, why pull requests are disabled, how outside agents send issues with diffs or AGENT-REVIEW.md feedback, and how credit works.

pages.title: Licensing and Security
pages.purpose: AGPL-3.0 with Apache-2.0 and MIT packages, trademarks, SECURITY.md disclosure, the public secret scan and telemetry disclosure.

pages.title: Deciding What Needs a Person
pages.purpose: How Tedix separates decisions that need a person from work it can finish alone: risk levels, budgets, triage of agent turns, and how only the valuable decisions reach a human.

pages.title: Approvals Before Risky Steps
pages.purpose: Approval requests, who may approve, why nobody approves their own request, approving with edited fields, and how approvals resume work.

pages.title: Decisions and Activity
pages.purpose: Decisions, waiting for a person, and Activity, the finished results: how cards are selected, ranked, dated and expired, and how they appear in Tedix OS and inside Claude and ChatGPT.

pages.title: Learning From Decisions
pages.purpose: How decisions and corrections become lessons and memory so the same question does not reach a person twice: lesson distillation, delivery into agent sessions, and memory recall.

pages.title: Work Items
pages.purpose: The unit of handed-off work: lifecycle from proposed to settled, attempts and leases, evidence, delegation between sessions, and the tedix work commands.

pages.title: Agent Sessions and Identity
pages.purpose: Verified agent sessions for Claude Code, Codex and other harnesses, one identity per tedi, and how actions are attributed to a session.

pages.title: Tedix CLI
pages.purpose: packages/cli: login and workspaces, tedix ask, tedix work, tedix code, and machine-readable output.

pages.title: CLI Hooks for Coding Agents
pages.purpose: Session-start, prompt-context and stop hooks for Claude Code, Codex and other hosts; what context they inject; what they send and when it is opt-in.

pages.title: CLI Authentication
pages.purpose: OAuth login, stored credentials, token refresh and file locking across processes, and scope inspection.

pages.title: Plugins for Claude, ChatGPT and Codex
pages.purpose: plugins/tedix: manifests, skills, hooks and how the public plugin repository is generated and validated for each host.

pages.title: MCP Gateway
pages.purpose: apps/mcp: the remote MCP server at connect.mcp.tedix.dev, how organization tools are aggregated, and how clients connect over OAuth.

pages.title: Code Mode
pages.purpose: Discovering and calling tools with JavaScript through discover.search and discover.describe, result limits, and completion evidence.

pages.title: Scopes and Authorization
pages.purpose: Capability scopes, risk tiers on tools, and how a call is authorized for an organization.

pages.title: Tool Catalog
pages.purpose: Tool rows in D1, schema sync from contracts, app installation per organization, and verb-first tool naming.

pages.title: API Service
pages.purpose: apps/api: oRPC routers, the contracts in packages/api-contract, and how services are organised.

pages.title: Jobs and Workflows
pages.purpose: Scheduled jobs, Cloudflare Workflows, queues, and how long-running work is resumed.

pages.title: Data on D1
pages.purpose: packages/db: Drizzle schema and query modules, migrations, batch instead of transactions, and the rules that keep queries safe in D1 batches.

pages.title: Billing and Credits
pages.purpose: Compute metering, the credit wallet and entitlements.

pages.title: Tedi Runtime
pages.purpose: apps/tedi-runtime: the Durable Object that runs a tedi, conversation and model selection, execution evidence and failure handling.

pages.title: Skills
pages.purpose: Skill definitions, the skill runtime, skill lifecycle and catalog data, and how a skill run produces results.

pages.title: Tedix OS Web App
pages.purpose: apps/os: routes, fixture-data development mode, and the main surfaces people use.

pages.title: Workspaces and Outputs
pages.purpose: Workspaces, resources and sharing, and Outputs (documents, sheets and presentations) with revisions and collaboration proposals.

pages.title: Apps and Widgets
pages.purpose: MCP App views, widgets and canvas, and how apps render inside Tedix OS and agent hosts.

pages.title: Running on Your Own Cloudflare Account
pages.purpose: Installation manifests, the self-hosted boundary, what is supported, and what stays with Tedix Cloud.
